HM-CONN-05.title: Sign-in options
HM-CONN-05.intro: Slack, Notion and some other services only let apps that keep a secret sign in. A relay keeps that secret and swaps your sign-in code for your tokens, which come back encrypted for this phone. The relay keeps nothing.
HM-CONN-05.ownNote: Run Hermit's open-source relay on a server you control and paste its address here. Only you and your server see your sign-ins.
HM-CONN-05.checkNone: This relay answered, but it doesn't sign in to any service yet.
HM-CONN-05.error.bad_address: Use an https address on a public server. Addresses on your home network, like 192.168.x.x or names ending in .local, aren't allowed.

HM-CONN-05.error.not_a_relay: Something answered at this address, but it isn't a Hermit relay.
HM-CONN-05.dojoNote: Off by default. If you turn it on, those sign-ins pass through Dojo's open-source relay, and Dojo would see which service you sign in to and when. It never sees your password, holds your tokens only long enough to encrypt them for this phone, and stores nothing.
HM-CONN-05.privacyNote: The relays you choose are listed on the privacy screen, with every time Hermit contacts them.
HM-CONN-05.introAll: How Hermit signs in to your accounts: with your own client, or through a relay for the services that need one.
HM-CONN-05.clientsNote: Gmail and Outlook can sign in with your own OAuth client from Google Cloud or Microsoft Entra, without depending on Dojo's. It's a public ID, not a secret.
HM-CONN-05.clientHelp.google: In Google Cloud, create an Android client for the package {package}, with the SHA-1 fingerprint of the key that signed this app, and in its advanced settings turn on Enable custom URI scheme.

HM-SET-09.title: What Hermit can use
HM-SET-09.intro: Everything Hermit can read or do, in one list. Anything that leaves the phone can never be set to Always.
HM-SET-09.searchSub: The first search in each chat asks you.
HM-SET-09.emailSub: Sending, replying, forwarding, archiving and saving drafts always ask you. So does reading your email.
HM-SET-09.rowSub: Permissions, what always asks, sites and connections
HM-SET-09.siteNote: Always: the site stays signed in after each task. Ask: Hermit clears its cookies and signs in again. Filling a saved login always asks for your {biometric}.
HM-SET-10.title: Device lab
HM-SET-10.rowSub: Measure Hermit on this phone, offline
HM-SET-10.intro: Measure how fast and how accurately Hermit runs on this phone. It should take about 10 minutes, and it works offline. Nothing is sent: at the end you see the report and decide whether to share it.
HM-SET-10.whatFacts: Reads what this phone is: maker and model, chip if the phone names it, memory, system version and processor cores.
HM-SET-10.whatSpeed: Times the model with a few thread counts: how fast it writes and how soon the first word comes.
HM-SET-10.whatEval: Runs {count} practice requests, test sentences that come with Hermit, and checks the first action it picks.
HM-SET-10.keepOpen: Keep Hermit open on this screen. The screen stays on while the lab runs, and if the phone gets hot the lab pauses until it cools down.
HM-SET-10.batterySaver: Battery saver is on, so this phone runs slower than usual. The report says so. Turn it off for numbers you can compare.
HM-SET-10.noModel: The model isn't on this phone yet. Download it first, then come back.
HM-SET-10.androidOnly: The Device lab runs on Android phones and iPhones only.
HM-SET-10.busy: Hermit is answering in the chat. Start the lab when it's done.
HM-SET-10.paused: Paused: the phone is hot. The lab goes on when it cools down.
HM-SET-10.leaveNote: Leaving this screen stops the lab.
HM-SET-10.stopped: Stopped. Nothing was kept or sent.
HM-SET-10.failed.too_hot: The phone stayed hot for 15 minutes, so the lab stopped. Let it cool down and try again.
HM-SET-10.failed.left: Hermit left the screen, so the lab stopped. Keep Hermit open while it runs.
HM-SET-10.failed.load: The model couldn't load, so the lab stopped.
HM-SET-10.failed.model: The model stopped answering, so the lab stopped.
HM-SET-10.failed.facts: Hermit couldn't read this phone's details, so the lab didn't start.
HM-SET-10.failed.unknown: Something went wrong and the lab stopped. Nothing was sent.
HM-SET-10.reportIntro: This is everything in the report, in plain words. Nothing has left the phone.
HM-SET-10.memoryLow: {gb} GB, a low-memory phone for Android
HM-SET-10.featuresNone: None of the ones the model uses
HM-SET-10.tier.unsupported: plan for phones below the minimum
HM-SET-10.never: Your name, accounts, contacts, messages, location or anything you typed, the name you gave the phone, and no number that identifies it, like its serial number or IMEI.
HM-SET-10.exactNote: This is exactly the text that Copy, Share and File it on GitHub use.
HM-SET-10.shareBody: Reports from many phones help tune Hermit's speed and accuracy for each one. File it on GitHub opens the Hermit project's report form in your browser with the report filled in. Nothing is filed until you press Submit there, and you need a GitHub account.
HM-SET-10.longCopied: The report is too long for a link, so it's copied: paste it into the form's Report field.
HM-SET-10.openFailed: Couldn't open the browser. Copy the report and file it at {address}.
